title: Teething: Signs and Safe Soothing
hook: Teething often starts around 6 months, but the timing varies a lot. Expect drooling, gum-rubbing, and fussiness — not a high fever, which points to something else.
key_points: Timing varies widely; first teeth often arrive around 6 months, but earlier or later is normal.
Typical signs: drooling, gum-rubbing or chewing, and mild fussiness that usually passes in a few days.
Soothe safely with a chilled (not frozen) teether, a clean cold washcloth, or a gentle gum massage with your finger.
Skip benzocaine teething gels and amber necklaces — the FDA warns of choking, strangulation, and other harms.
content_html: Teething tends to begin somewhere around six months, though some babies start earlier and others later — wide variation is completely normal. The usual signs are drooling, a baby who wants to rub or chew on their gums, and some extra fussiness. For many babies it causes little or no trouble, and any discomfort generally passes within a few days.
extra_html: For relief, the AAP suggests safe, simple options: a chilled (not rock-hard frozen) teether, a clean cold washcloth to gnaw on, or gently massaging the sore gums with a clean finger. Two things to avoid: numbing gels containing benzocaine, which the FDA does not recommend for infants because of choking and other risks, and amber teething necklaces, which the FDA warns can cause choking and strangulation and have no proven benefit. One more important point — teething does not cause a high fever. If your baby spikes a fever, assume something else is going on. This is general guidance; talk to your pediatrician about soothing options and any symptoms that worry you.

related.title: Motor Milestones: Rolling to Crawling
related.hook: In the first year babies move through a rough sequence — rolling, sitting, crawling, pulling to stand — but the timing varies widely, and ranges matter more than exact dates.

related.title: Common Rashes in Babies and Kids
related.hook: Most childhood rashes — diaper rash, eczema, heat rash, hand-foot-and-mouth — are common and harmless. There's one big exception worth memorizing: a rash that doesn't fade when you press it.

related.title: Caring for the First Teeth
related.hook: Baby teeth matter — they hold space for adult teeth and shape eating and speech. Brushing starts with the very first tooth, and the first dental visit comes earlier than most parents expect.

flashcards.prompt: Which is a safe way to soothe a teething baby?

choices.text: A chilled (not frozen) teether or a gentle gum massage
A benzocaine numbing gel rubbed on the gums
An amber teething necklace worn all day

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP recommends cold, safe objects and gum massage. It warns against benzocaine gels and teething necklaces because of choking and strangulation risks.

flashcards.prompt: If a teething baby develops a high fever, what should you assume?
flashcards.back_html: Not teething. Teething may cause mild fussiness and drooling, but a high fever needs another explanation — check in with your pediatrician.
